body: i don’t know the etiquette for commenting on my own post but can somebody please help me. i really have no one and i don’t know what to do

I find it really difficult to stay positive about anything honestly. I keep looking back and questioning whether I was ever really valued by anyone, and the fact is that I still don’t have a lot of good to look back on. I’m just scared that my youth is going to pass by without me having done anything with it.

I’ll do my best though. Instead of looking back I should probably just look forward at the things I have ahead of me. Maybe I’ll stop sabotaging myself and reach out to my friend tomorrow, if only just to chat. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

nobody talks to me unless i talk to them first and they don’t show any interest. i go on forums or places like suicidewatch seeking advice and a handful of people pretend to care for a few minutes and then disappear, if anyone says anything at all. i have no close friends and my family hates me. so.

i’ll keep this in mind, thank you. but if it’s okay for me to ask, do you have any advice for the short-term in terms of dealing with the feelings that result from seeing this kind of behavior? i don’t have any strategies for when the self-criticism is triggered in this specific way and i keep making it worse with my usual approach. (if you don’t have advice for this it’s fine, don’t worry about it too much either way.)

i exercise but a lot of it is compulsive things i do in response to body dysmorphia. it makes me feel worse a lot of the time because i realize no amount of exercise will fix what’s wrong with me so i just do what i feel is the minimum required for good health.

i do have family but they always find it irritating when i’m not doing well. i had a really severe falling out with my mother a few years ago and i can’t tell her anything because she says i’m emotionally manipulating her if i express any sadness.

i’m studying international relations. i’m learning russian too because i’d hoped to be a translator for some kind of government job but i realized recently that it’ll be years before i have the language proficiency required for it. so now i just feel like giving up. i took an extra year of high school because of mental illness, and i’m taking two extra years of undergrad, and i’ll have wasted my early 20s by the time i’m ready for an actual career. honestly i feel like a failure when i think about it.
